name: config/urls.py
summary: Root URL configuration module for the conversationalBI Django project that maps incoming HTTP request paths to their corresponding view handlers and application sub-routers.
purpose: Acts as the central routing table for the Django backend, defining how incoming HTTP requests are dispatched to the appropriate views or included app-level URL configurations. It ensures a single, maintainable entry point for all web traffic and enforces separation between request routing and business logic.
responsibilities: Define the top-level urlpatterns list that Django's URL resolver traverses
Route incoming HTTP request paths to the correct application views or sub-URL configurations
Include and mount app-specific URL modules using django.urls.include for modularity
Expose the Django admin interface via django.contrib.admin
Provide named URL patterns to support reverse URL resolution throughout the project
inputs: Incoming HTTP request paths and methods from the WSGI/ASGI server
App-level URL configuration modules to be included
Django URL resolver path matching requests
outputs: Resolved view functions or class-based view instances
Delegated routing to included app-level URLconfs
HTTP 404 responses for paths that do not match any defined pattern
architecture_notes: This module serves as the Root URLconf implementing the Front Controller pattern. By importing include, path, and admin, it follows standard Django conventions for a multi-app architecture: the root router handles high-level path prefixes (such as admin/ or api/) and delegates detailed routing to individual apps. This decouples the project-level routing table from application internals, allowing teams to own their URL namespaces independently and preventing the root urls.py from becoming a bottleneck during parallel development.
improvements: Add explicit path() entries to include each sub-application's urls.py (e.g., path('api/', include('api.urls'))) to activate modular routing
Introduce API versioning prefixes (e.g., path('api/v1/', ...)) to future-proof REST endpoints
Add a root-level health-check or ping endpoint for load balancer and monitoring integration
Include static() and media() URL patterns for local development if not already handled
Define custom handler404 and handler500 references at the module level for centralized error management
Consider mounting an API schema endpoint (e.g., OpenAPI/Swagger) if the project exposes a REST interface
